correctness.rationale: Orbits of the full permutation are mapped equivariantly and injectively; choosing k source and target cycles, a bijection, and ℓ independent phase shifts gives the exact count. The missing-cycle weights have ratio (m-j)/(ℓ(j+1)^2). Dominated convergence gives the total-variation Bessel limit, and two geometric tail comparisons around √(m/ℓ) prove supercritical concentration. Actual exhaustive checker on up to six points and numerical critical limits passed; finite tests are not used as infinite proofs.

value.rationale: The family of centralizers is canonical for a cyclic permutation action. The dimensionless ratio m/ℓ controls a sharp three-regime domain-defect transition, yielding a nondegenerate discrete-Bessel critical distribution and a square-root law outside it. This is a natural asymptotic statistic about the density of units versus nonunits in a whole family, not a reprint of a table or arbitrary small finite case.
